questions.prompt: In Eucharistic Prayer II, the priest prays 'Make holy these gifts, we pray, by sending down your Spirit upon them like the dewfall.' This moment is called the epiclesis. Per CCC 1353, why is it theologically necessary?
choices: It invokes the Holy Spirit's power to change the bread and wine and to unite the communicants, since the Spirit's action, not human words alone, effects the consecration
It is a purely decorative prayer with no doctrinal significance
It replaces the need for the Words of Institution
It is unique to Eucharistic Prayer II and has no equivalent in the other prayers
questions.correctAnswer: It invokes the Holy Spirit's power to change the bread and wine and to unite the communicants, since the Spirit's action, not human words alone, effects the consecration
questions.explanation: CCC 1353 describes the epiclesis as the Church's petition asking the Father to send the Holy Spirit so that the offerings may become the Body and Blood of Christ, and so that the communicants may be made one body and one spirit -- the whole Eucharistic Prayer is Trinitarian, not a human action alone.
questions.hint: This prayer calls specifically on the Third Person of the Trinity, not a general blessing.

citations.quote: In the epiclesis, the Church asks the Father to send his Holy Spirit... on the bread and wine, so that by his power they may become the body and blood of Jesus Christ and so that those who take part in the Eucharist may be one body and one spirit.

questions.prompt: The Roman Canon's 'Unde et memores' ('Therefore, O Lord, as we celebrate the memorial...') is the Mass's anamnesis. How does anamnesis differ from the epiclesis that comes before it in the same prayer?
choices: Anamnesis is the Church's act of remembering and making present Christ's Paschal Mystery; epiclesis is the invocation calling down the Holy Spirit
Anamnesis and epiclesis are two names for the exact same prayer
Anamnesis only occurs in the Eastern liturgies, never in the Roman Rite
Epiclesis is the priest's personal reflection, while anamnesis is the congregation's spoken response
questions.correctAnswer: Anamnesis is the Church's act of remembering and making present Christ's Paschal Mystery; epiclesis is the invocation calling down the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: The epiclesis calls on the Holy Spirit to consecrate the gifts; the anamnesis that follows is the Church's remembrance -- not a mere mental recollection, but a liturgical act that makes Christ's saving death and resurrection present -- of the Paschal Mystery being celebrated.
questions.hint: One prayer calls on a divine Person; the other recalls a saving event.

citations.quote: The celebration 'makes a remembrance' of the marvelous works of God in an anamnesis which may be more or less developed.

questions.prompt: True or False: The General Instruction of the Roman Missal's (GIRM) rubrics on posture (standing, kneeling, sitting) and vesture exist purely as arbitrary custom, with no rationale connected to what is happening liturgically at each moment.
questions.explanation: GIRM rubrics encode theological meaning: standing during the Gospel honors Christ's own words, kneeling during the Eucharistic Prayer expresses adoration, and specific vestments (like the priest's chasuble) signify the minister's sacred role rather than his private identity. These norms are deliberate, not arbitrary.
questions.hint: Ask what each posture or vestment expresses about the specific moment it belongs to.

citations.reference: General Instruction of the Roman Missal, art. 42-43

questions.prompt: Canon 849 of the Code of Canon Law establishes that Baptism is validly conferred using water, with the correct form of words invoking the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit -- water is the sacrament's ____, and the Trinitarian formula is its form.
questions.explanation: Every sacrament requires valid matter (the physical element or action) and form (the words that specify its meaning) -- for Baptism, canon 849 specifies water as the matter and the Trinitarian invocation as the form, both required together for validity.
questions.hint: This is the physical element used, as distinguished from the words spoken over it.

citations.quote: Baptism... is validly conferred only by a washing of true water with the proper form of words.

questions.prompt: Which canonical hour of the Divine Office traditionally includes the Magnificat (Mary's canticle from Luke 1:46-55) as its Gospel canticle?
choices: Vespers (Evening Prayer)
Lauds (Morning Prayer)
Compline (Night Prayer)
The Office of Readings
questions.explanation: Vespers, the Church's evening prayer, traditionally includes the Magnificat as its Gospel canticle, just as Lauds includes the Benedictus (Zechariah's canticle, Luke 1:68-79) -- each hour's canticle is chosen to fit its place in the daily rhythm of prayer.
questions.hint: This is the evening counterpart to Lauds's morning canticle, the Benedictus.

questions.prompt: Match each liturgical term to its precise meaning.

pairs.right: The invocation calling down the Holy Spirit upon the gifts
The Church's act of remembering and making present the Paschal Mystery
The seasons built around specific mysteries of Christ, e.g. Advent, Lent, Easter
The remaining weeks of the year, celebrating the mystery of Christ in its fullness rather than one specific aspect

questions.explanation: Sacrosanctum Concilium 102-105 distinguishes proper time, which unfolds specific mysteries across the liturgical year, from Ordinary Time, which celebrates the whole mystery of Christ without emphasizing one particular aspect -- both are integral to the calendar, not a 'default' versus a 'special' season.
questions.hint: One column of terms belongs to the Eucharistic Prayer specifically; the other belongs to the calendar.

questions.prompt: What is the specific function of the 'epiclesis' in the Eucharistic Prayer?
choices: A calling-down of the Holy Spirit upon the gifts, and upon the assembly, so the offering becomes what it signifies
A recitation of the day's saint
A blessing given only at the very end of Mass
A private prayer said silently before Mass begins
questions.correctAnswer: A calling-down of the Holy Spirit upon the gifts, and upon the assembly, so the offering becomes what it signifies
questions.explanation: The epiclesis makes explicit that the consecration is the Spirit's work, not a formula operating automatically apart from the Trinity's action. Eastern liturgies place particular emphasis here; the West includes it too, though its precise placement developed differently across the two traditions.
questions.hint: The Greek root concerns 'calling upon' — ask who is being called upon, and for what.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Roman Canon (Eucharistic Prayer I) is the oldest Eucharistic Prayer still in regular use in the Roman Rite.
questions.explanation: True. Its core text dates to roughly the fourth century and it remained the Roman Rite's only Eucharistic Prayer for many centuries before others were introduced after Vatican II, which is part of why its language and structure differ noticeably from the newer options.
questions.hint: This prayer predates the other Eucharistic Prayers commonly used today by many centuries.

questions.prompt: According to Canon 849, what is the minimum required for a valid Baptism?
choices: Real water, and the Trinitarian formula 'I baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit'
A priest and a church building
Water and the recitation of the Creed
Oil, water, and a full catechetical program completed beforehand
questions.correctAnswer: Real water, and the Trinitarian formula 'I baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit'
questions.explanation: This minimal requirement is precisely why any person, in an emergency, can validly baptize — a nurse, a stranger, anyone — using ordinary water and the correct words, even absent a priest or any building at all.
questions.hint: Ask what would still make a baptism valid even performed by a layperson in an emergency.
